brief.description: A low brick-and-timber tannery with a real open vat, rear drying rack and integrated front controller.
brief.purpose: Make the hide-to-leather workshop recognizable as a practical wet craft beside the Textile Workshop and Smithy.
brief.silhouette: Three blocks wide and three deep: low rectangular vat and work rim in front, paired narrow timber posts and one rear crossbar above it; broad negative space through the rack.
brief.bounds: Controller at front-center; assembly stays within x=-1..1, depth=0..2 and no more than four blocks high.
brief.materials: Vanilla/resource-pack brick and oak construction, restrained copper only for vat lining or drain, dark iron and leather-colored controller details.
brief.interfaces: Existing front-center controller, contextual guide, coal processing and inventory behavior remain unchanged.
brief.states: Static structure; controller retains existing working/fire state behavior and shared UI.
brief.construction: Existing bricks, planks, copper and saw-cut slabs/beams/eighth cubes; no new decorative block or entity.
brief.invariants: No recipe, production, capacity, fuel or inventory changes. No required water, loose hide prop or invented mechanism.
brief.technological_stage: Frontier craft becoming organized town industry.
brief.material_behavior: Rough brick plinth, directional oak grain, darker wet-vat recess, restrained oxidizable copper detail.
brief.signature_feature: Low open tanning vat beneath a supported rear drying rack.
brief.neighboring_assets: Textile Workshop, Smithy, Raw Hide and Cloth.
fidelity_targets: Vat occupies most of the low 3x2 working mass without becoming a solid box.
Two narrow rear posts and one top crossbar remain visibly supported and leave an open center.
Partial blocks create rim, posts and feet instead of full-block columns.
Front-center controller reads as part of the brick/timber assembly.

references.role: Frozen assembly and exact Minecraft material context; the revised tannery is at right.
Project multiblock presentation and partial-block construction language only.

generations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: implementable Minecraft multiblock design reference
Primary request: Redesign the Civilization Tannery as one coherent, attractive late-nineteenth-century workshop assembly.
Input images: Image 1 is the current in-game workshop lineup and material/scale context; redesign only the tannery shown at right. Image 2 is presentation and partial-block construction language only, not a shape to copy.
Subject: A three-block-wide, three-block-deep tannery with the controller at bottom front center. Build a low brick plinth and genuinely open rectangular tanning vat with a thin oak work rim, supported narrow oak posts at the rear, and one strong top drying-rack crossbar. Use a few restrained copper lining/drain details where physically useful. The rack center remains open and visibly supported.
Style/medium: polished Minecraft build mockup using feasible full blocks, slabs, quarter beams and eighth cubes; 32x resource-pack material density; late nineteenth-century practical craft.
Composition/framing: side-by-side front three-quarter and rear three-quarter views of the same isolated assembly on a neutral stone floor, matching scale and orientation.
Materials/textures: red brick, warm oak, dark iron controller fittings, small functional copper details. Clear directional wood grain and masonry joints.
Constraints: exact maximum footprint 3x3 blocks, maximum height 4 blocks, controller at front-center, major pieces aligned to Minecraft half-block geometry, broad negative space, buildable with existing brick/oak/copper cut pieces. No new gameplay component.
Avoid: solid 3x3 blob, full-block timber pillars, railings, ladders, decorative gears, pipes, modern equipment, floating hides, water simulation, people, labels, impossible curves, tiny ornamental clutter.

Use case: stylized-concept refinement
Asset type: implementable Minecraft multiblock design reference
Primary request: Preserve the selected Civilization Tannery direction from Image 1, but redraw it as a mechanically exact, feasible 3x3 Minecraft assembly informed by the actual blockout in Image 2.
Reference roles: Image 1 is the selected design and owns silhouette/material hierarchy. Image 2 is the actual current implementation and owns exact scale, footprint, cut-block geometry and controller placement. Image 3 is partial-block presentation language only.
Subject: A low one-block red-brick 3x3 plinth, a half-height oak rim around a genuinely open vat center, two narrow rear oak posts, and one three-block-wide half-grid oak crossbar. Controller at bottom front center. Keep the existing custom controller identity but do not show liquids, loose hides, pipes, or extra machines.
Style: polished Minecraft build mockup, Faithful 32x material density, practical late-nineteenth-century frontier industry.
Composition: side-by-side front three-quarter and rear three-quarter views of the same isolated assembly on neutral stone.
Constraints: exact 3x3 footprint, maximum four blocks high; only full blocks, slabs, quarter beams and eighth cubes; all parts visibly supported; same asset in both views.
Avoid: solid tall blob, full-width posts, floating fittings, copper vat lining, water, people, text, modern equipment, decorative gears.

criteria.silhouette_scale: The low 3x3 brick vat and narrow rear timber rack produce a clear wet-workshop silhouette with broad open space above the basin.
criteria.implementable_geometry: The brick base, half-height rim, quarter-beam posts and top crossbar translate directly to the existing saw-cut block system; the illustration's small metal drain becomes controller-face detail rather than a new component.
criteria.mechanics_clearance: The vat center is open, both rack posts are grounded on the rim and the crossbar spans between supports without floating pieces.
criteria.period_materials: Brick, oak and restrained dark metal fit a late-nineteenth-century frontier tannery and remain visually distinct from the timber textile bench.
criteria.family_consistency: Its partial-block supports and readable construction share the Smithy's hand-built town-workshop language without copying its hearth form.
criteria.controls_readability: The front-center controller remains exposed and visually integrated below the work rim.
criteria.gameplay_scope: The design changes only structure geometry and artwork; water, loose hides and extra mechanisms shown or implied by the craft are not added to gameplay.
